classification.difficultyReason: Identify matching triangles and select SSS, SAS or AAS using marked givens, common sides, equal radii and vertically opposite angles, then deduce corresponding equal sides or angles. Parts c and d require choosing the triangles, but congruence is explicitly directed and no auxiliary construction is needed.

spec.description: Triangle ABC with interior M, three spokes, triple ticks on AB and AC, double ticks on BM and CM, and apex angles alpha and beta.

answer.worked:
In triangles $ABM$ and $ACM$:
$$\begin{aligned}AB&=AC&&\text{(given)}\\AM&=AM&&\text{(common)}\\BM&=CM&&\text{(given)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle ABM\equiv\triangle ACM$ (SSS).
$\angle BAM=\angle CAM$ because matching angles of congruent triangles are equal. Hence $\alpha=\beta$.

spec.description: A, O, P are collinear; B, O, Q are collinear. Right angles at A and P, double ticks on AO and OP, x on AB and y on PQ.
spec.mathematics: OA=OP; angle OAB=angle OPQ=90 degrees; vertically opposite angles at O.

answer.worked:
In triangles $OAB$ and $OPQ$:
$$\begin{aligned}OA&=OP&&\text{(given)}\\\angle AOB&=\angle POQ&&\text{(vertically opposite angles)}\\\angle OAB&=\angle OPQ=90^\circ&&\text{(given)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle OAB\equiv\triangle OPQ$ (AAS).
$AB=PQ$ because matching sides of congruent triangles are equal. Hence $x=y$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Use congruence to prove that $FG=GH$, given that $O$ is the centre of the circle.

spec.description: Circle with centre O, radii OF, OG and OH, chords FG and GH, and equal central angles alpha. Ordinary source blue strokes and the centre marker use house black.
spec.mathematics: OF=OH as radii; OG is common; angle FOG=angle HOG.

answer.short:
$\triangle GOF\equiv\triangle GOH$ (SAS), so $FG=GH$.

Matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.
answer.worked:
In triangles $GOF$ and $GOH$:
$$\begin{aligned}OG&=OG&&\text{(common)}\\OF&=OH&&\text{(radii)}\\\angle FOG&=\angle HOG=\alpha&&\text{(given)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle GOF\equiv\triangle GOH$ (SAS). Hence $FG=GH$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).

children.label: d
children.prompt: Use congruence to prove that $AD=DC$ and that $AB=BC$.

spec.description: Quadrilateral ABCD with horizontal diagonal BD; 80-degree angles at A and C and 70-degree angles at B on both sides of BD.
spec.mathematics: BD is common; angle ABD=angle CBD=70 degrees; angle DAB=angle DCB=80 degrees.

answer.short:
$\triangle DAB\equiv\triangle DCB$ (AAS), so $AD=DC$ and $AB=BC$.

Matching sides of congruent triangles are equal.
answer.worked:
In triangles $DAB$ and $DCB$:
$$\begin{aligned}BD&=BD&&\text{(common)}\\\angle ABD&=\angle CBD=70^\circ&&\text{(given)}\\\angle DAB&=\angle DCB=80^\circ&&\text{(given)}\end{aligned}$$
Therefore $\triangle DAB\equiv\triangle DCB$ (AAS). Hence $AD=DC$ and $AB=BC$ (matching sides of congruent triangles).
